_note: Copy to docs/work/checklist/<yyyy-mm-dd>-<subject>.json. Never fill this file in place. status is pass|fail|skipped|substituted; substituted means checked by a different instrument than the item names, and its reason must say which. accepted stays null until a human answers it, so an unfinished run is visibly unfinished. Delete any item whose feature no longer exists rather than skipping it.

findings-against-prior-runs.so-what: The skill's example query is not strictly overlap-free (stopword); use the 'inside' variant.

findings-against-prior-runs.prior-claim: note-opening-chunk-reports-index-zero: the 62-paragraph minutes note produces 8 rows (indices 0..7)
findings-against-prior-runs.what-is-actually-true: On 1.56.1 the same fixture is 2 rows (4303 + 3015 chars), consistent with the 2026-10-02 run's 2 rows; chunk sizing changed since 1.53.13 so the 'last index = 7 of 8' wording in the item is stale (the regression would now be 1 of 2).
findings-against-prior-runs.so-what: Item text could cite a scaled fixture (e.g. 300 paragraphs, 9 rows per 10-02 run) to make the index-0 check more discriminating.

findings-against-prior-runs.what-is-actually-true: No prior claim found wrong. A word after the 64th distinct word loses its fts leg on 1.56.1 and keeps it on 1.56.0; repeats do not consume the cap; a 6-token query keeps its stopword 'the', a 71-token one drops it. DEFECT: two caller-facing strings shipped in 1.56.1 still claim the keyword leg sees the whole query. CodeSearchWarnings.QueryTrimmedToCodeWindow ('keyword matching still saw it in full') is appended to the new memory warning, so one warning contradicts itself whenever kind includes code (the default here); MemoryTools.cs:145's query parameter description ('Keyword matching still covers the query in full') is what every client reads in tools/list. Code search shares FtsQueryNormalizer.BuildPlan (SqliteCodeSearchService.cs:32), and a query long enough to pass the 510-token code window is far over 64 words, so both claims are false.
items.acceptance-reason: Proposed: accept as a tracked defect. The behaviour passes: the cap, the latency and the ranking boundary each went red on 1.56.0 and green on 1.56.1. The two stale strings are fixed in PR #844 (fix/keyword-cap-wording), which ships with the next release.

items.expected-result: Watch a scratch directory (`settings ingest scope add`, `settings watch enable`, memory_watch_add) holding x.md, w.md and y.md, plus node_modules/pkg/index.md and .git/notes.md, each with a term found nowhere else. Wait for three watch_files rows, `chmod 000` node_modules, wait 2 s, then edit y.md so watches.last_change_ts moves past x.md's watch_files.updated_at. Read both values while the server runs, because a stopped WAL bank will not open read-only. Stop the server. Replace one word of x.md with a new term of the same byte length and `touch -t $(date -r <t> +%Y%m%d%H%M.%S)` it, where t is between x.md's updated_at and last_change_ts. Rewrite w.md at a different size with a new term, and touch it to before its own updated_at. Restart on the same data root. Within seconds memory_search finds both new terms, watch_files shows new updated_at and size for x.md and w.md, and memory_watch_status reads Healthy. Neither the node_modules term nor the .git term is ever found. Premise: before the restart, updated_at(x.md) <= mtime(x.md) <= last_change_ts. A build without ADR-0121 finds neither new term, because it re-queues only files with mtime > last_change_ts. The 5-minute heal pass (WatchHostedService.HealInterval, event 322 at Debug) is optional: it needs a server left up for over 5 minutes (ADR-0121)
items.command: w1.sh (as above) then w2.sh: chmod 000 wdir/node_modules; sleep 3; rewrite y.md; sleep 6; sqlite3 -readonly (while server up) 'select last_change_ts from watches; select path,updated_at,size from watch_files'; stat. w3.sh: kill 67169; sed x.md xylophoneaaa->xylophonebbb (same length); touch -t $(date -r 1791042095 ...) x.md; rewrite w.md (35->78 bytes, term walrusnewterm777); touch w.md to epoch 1791042000; nohup serve on same data root (new port 61399, pid 73535); sleep 12. w4.sh/search.py: memory_search (projectId wproj, scope all, sessionId lanec) for each term; sqlite3 -readonly watch_files; memory_watch_status.

After edits: x.md mtime=1791042095 size=35 (1791042089 <= 1791042095 <= 1791042106 holds), w.md mtime=1791042000 size=78 (< its updated_at 1791042089). After restart: search xylophonebbb -> hit path .../wdir/x.md snippet '# X\n\nAlpha note xylophonebbb here.' chunkIndex 0; walrusnewterm777 -> hit w.md snippet '...carrying walrusnewterm777 and extra words.'; xylophoneaaa, walrusold111, nmzzzterm, gitzzzterm -> results: []; watch_files after: x.md|1791042129|35, y.md|1791042106|43, w.md|1791042129|78; memory_watch_status state Healthy lastSync 2026-10-03T15:42:09.966019+00:00. Control: y.md term yakyakyak found.
items.observed-result: Both missed changes healed on restart within the 12 s wait: x.md (same size, mtime inside [updated_at,last_change_ts], which only ADR-0121's fingerprint rule catches) and w.md (size changed, mtime older than its own updated_at). New terms found, old terms gone, updated_at moved to 1791042129 for exactly those two while untouched y.md kept 1791042106. node_modules (chmod 000) and .git terms never found. The optional 5-minute heal pass (event 322, Debug) was not exercised: server not left up >5 min, and Debug lines are not logged at default level. Not run: a pre-ADR-0121 build as negative control.
items.acceptance-reason: Proposed: accept: judged by x.md's and w.md's own fingerprints (watch_files rows) plus search; the same-length/in-window edit is the case a mtime>last_change_ts rule misses.
